title: Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards: government response to report
description: The government's response to the Committee's 2020 report Artificial Intelligence and Public Standards
summary: The government has issued a response to the 2020 Committee report on artificial intelligence and public standards, outlining its stance on AI governance. It highlights commitments to strengthen accountability, promote transparency, and ensure that AI technologies serve the public interest.

title: EM on EU Regulation 2024/1689 on Artificial Intelligence
description: The government's summary of an EU regulation laying down harmonised rules on artificial intelligence and amending several Regulations and Directives.
summary: This document explains the EU Regulation 2024/1689, which establishes harmonised rules for artificial intelligence. It updates various existing regulations and directives to align with the new AI framework.

title: ​​Ofqual’s approach to regulating the use of artificial intelligence in the qualifications sector​
description: Published in response to a request from the Secretary of State for Education, the Secretary of State for Science, Innovation and Technology, and the Secretary of State for Business and Trade.
summary: Ofqual is setting out how it will monitor and control the use of artificial intelligence in exams and qualifications, aiming to keep assessments fair and reliable. The guidance was issued after a request from the Secretaries of State for Education, Science, Innovation and Technology, and Business and Trade.

title: Report and impact assessment on Copyright and Artificial Intelligence
description: A report and impact assessment on the use of copyright works in the development of artificial intelligence (AI) systems.
summary: This document evaluates how AI development utilizes copyrighted content, examining legal implications, ethical concerns, and the potential need for new licensing frameworks. It aims to guide policymakers and industry stakeholders in balancing innovation with the protection of intellectual property rights.

title: Government response to the House of Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence
description: Government response to the Lords Select Committee on Artificial Intelligence report ‘AI in the UK: No Room for Complacency’.
summary: The government’s reply outlines its commitment to keep pace with the rapid development of AI while ensuring safety, fairness and public trust, and it accepts most of the Committee’s recommendations to strengthen regulation and support for research. It also stresses the need to balance innovation with oversight, calling for clearer guidelines, stronger data protections, and investment in skills to build a responsible AI ecosystem in the UK.

title: AI and Public Standards – Terms of Reference
description: Terms of Reference and FAQs for the Committee's review into artificial intelligence and public standards.
summary: This document outlines the scope and objectives for a committee that will evaluate how artificial intelligence should be regulated and what public standards it should meet. It also provides frequently asked questions to guide members in understanding the process and key concerns.

title: CSPL submission to Science and Technology Committee inquiry on Governance of AI
description: CSPL has submitted written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee's inquiry on Governance of Artificial Intelligence.
summary: CSPL has provided written evidence to the Science and Technology Committee as part of its inquiry into the governance of Artificial Intelligence. The submission outlines the organization’s views and recommendations on how AI should be regulated and overseen.

title: Impact of AI on the regulation of medical products
description: Implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) White Paper principles.
summary: The document examines how artificial intelligence is changing the rules that govern medical products. It outlines steps for using AI White Paper principles to ensure safety, effectiveness, and accountability in medical device regulation.

title: Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy
description: Our vision is that, in terms of AI, we will be the world’s most effective, efficient, trusted and influential Defence organisation for our size.
summary: The Defence Artificial Intelligence Strategy is a plan to make the defence organisation the most effective, efficient, trusted, and influential AI player worldwide, given its size. It focuses on developing AI capabilities, fostering collaboration, and ensuring responsible and ethical use of AI in defence operations.

title: Transport artificial intelligence action plan
description: Sets out how DfT will work with the transport sector to exploit the opportunities from AI while managing potential risks.
summary: The Transport Artificial Intelligence Action Plan outlines how the Department for Transport will partner with the transport industry to harness the benefits of AI, such as improving safety and efficiency. It also details measures to identify, assess, and mitigate risks associated with AI deployments across the sector.
